description: The judge's whole answer about one repository, read from the summary it was given and nothing else. Every field is required and no other field is allowed.

kind.description: What kind of repository this is. Take the FIRST of these six that the summary shows, in this order. generated: a tool produced it wholesale and little of it is the author's own work. clone: a copy, or a lightly changed copy, of another project; say clone only on a sign the summary shows: the README describes another named project, or gives another project's repository, clone address or deployed site as this one's own; commit subjects merge from another repository or an upstream remote; most of the sampled code files carry another project's copyright or licence header; the history begins with one bulk import of most of the files. A clone is judged from a short summary, so when it shows no such sign it is not a clone. plan only: a plan or a specification with little or no running code. mixed: original work with real code and a substantial part that is plan or generated by a tool for this project. A third-party library, SDK, header set, driver package or board-generated code kept beside the author's own code never makes a repository mixed or a clone: judge the author's own code. own-work: original working code, including original code that bundles third-party libraries. built: use it only where the repository is working code and the summary cannot tell whose it is or how it came about; it is never the default for doubt between the others.

folders.description: Every folder the summary lists, each with the one class that fits it best, by its path as the summary gives it ('.' is the root). A file belongs to its most specific listed folder.

path.description: The folder's path as the summary gives it, relative to the repository root, with no leading slash and no '..'.

class.description: own code: the author's working code. own tests: the author's tests. own tooling: the author's build, scripts and configuration. docs: documentation. generated: output of a tool. vendored: another project's code kept here. reference: material kept to read, not to run. fixture data: sample inputs a test reads.

scores.description: The metrics that need judgment, each a 0 to 100 score with the judge's confidence and the evidence it rests on. Size and Maintainability's parts are counted by the kernel, Provenance is read from the history; none of them is asked here.

quality.description: Quality's review: correctness, tests, error handling and idiom, judged from the sampled files.

confidence.description: How sure the judge is of this score, 0 to 1.

evidence.description: What the score rests on: at least one short item, each a path or a quotation from the summary.

complexity.description: Complexity's assessment: the difficulty of the problem actually solved, not the size of the code.

confidence.description: How sure the judge is of this score, 0 to 1.

evidence.description: What the score rests on: at least one short item, each a path or a quotation from the summary.

navigability.description: AI navigability, judged by its mechanisms: instruction files, module boundaries, naming, tests an agent can run.

confidence.description: How sure the judge is of this score, 0 to 1.

evidence.description: What the score rests on: at least one short item, each a path or a quotation from the summary.

ambition.description: How hard the stated goal was, against the calibrated tiers.

tier.description: toy: a small exercise, demonstration, sample or template, or a project whose own working code is a few hundred lines. utility: a tool that does one useful job. product: a complete thing a person other than its author can pick up and use: an application, a game, an instrument or a device, a site or a service; a single-purpose tool, bot, script or library that does one job for a developer is a utility, however polished. research: an attempt at something not yet known to work.

confidence.description: How sure the judge is of the tier, 0 to 1.

evidence.description: What the tier rests on: at least one short item, each a path or a quotation from the summary.

quality.description: Quality as the calibration labels give it, a whole number from 1 (poor) to 5 (excellent).

verdict.description: A short verdict in plain words, at most 400 characters.
